method: `score_iag_against_baker.py` finds the corrected IAG atlas 1.1% from Baker, Blake & Reiners 2020's telluric-free IAG Sun at telluric pixels, against their quoted 0.35%. Their atmosphere was removed by an empirical fit per line, so a line our list has wrong is right in theirs. This asks how much of the difference that is. Per fitted window, Baker's Sun replaces ours: it is aligned by the velocity the score found and put on the corrected spectrum's scale by a line fitted where nothing absorbs, so observed / it is the transmission the atlas saw (up to their error), and model / stellar model is ours. Then, per telluric feature of the strength table's catalogue (`tellurix_fts.line_depth`: AER H2O and O2 clusters, 8800-17600 cm-1), the same measurement the table was built from -- the optical depth ratio over the core pixels, and a shift-and-scale fit for its position -- now free of our solar model.
pixel_class_definition: core: within 0.05 cm-1 of a catalogue feature (S >= 3e-25); wing: 0.05-0.15 from one; weak line: elsewhere with model tau > 0.03; little absorption: the rest
